sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Air Freight Forwarding and Cargo Aircraft Charter

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic French Civil Code) with administrative law courts and hierarchical application of EU law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1967, as amended)
France–People's Republic of China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1984, supplemented 2013)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (2009, as adapted post-Brexit)
France–Hong Kong SAR Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1997)
France–Switzerland Double Taxation Convention (1966, as revised)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 (AML/CFT obligations); Code de commerce, Articles L.561-45 to L.561-52 and R.123-166 et seq. (French UBO register and beneficial ownership declaration); Décret n° 2016-1235 du 19 septembre 2016; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020 transposing EU Directive 2018/843; TRACFIN administrative guidance; ACPR and French Prudential Supervision regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or EU identity card of each shareholder, manager and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or police/consular authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-EU Hague Convention signatory countries; otherwise Consular Legalization through the French consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each proposed manager and UBO (utility bill or bank statement issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the issuer is a public or municipal entity; otherwise sworn French translation only

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Judicial record record extract / certificate of good conduct for each proposed manager (casier judiciaire or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official national criminal records authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague Convention countries; Consular Legalization for all other countries; sworn French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing for any corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or competent corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization plus sworn French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all UBOs and proposed managers against French and EU political exposure identifiers, FAITF-style indicators and TRAFICFIN typologies; mandatory international sanctions screening against French Gestban, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list for USD/EUR transactions, United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, and French domestic terrorist and anti- money-laundering prohibitions. Verification is required at formation, on any UBO or capital change, and at least annually where the SARL acts as an air cargo charter broker subject to customs and aviation authority review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises coordinated by INPI (Registre National des Entreprises) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; company name availability confirmed via Infogreffe and the Local Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French statutory mandatory documentation must be in French under the Loi Toubon (Act 94-665); the corporate name may include Latin-script foreign words provided it is phonetically equivalent and does not mislead the public; non-Roman scripts are transliterated into standard Roman alphabet; accents and diacritics are permitted; the name must be represented in French including all mandatory legal notices and the RCS extract.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or the Guichet unique rejects the chosen corporate name, the applicant may within 30 calendar days of the refusal file a written recours gracieux with the same registry officer requesting reconsideration; if that is unsuccessful, appeal may be made to the judge supervising the RCS registry (juge commis à la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés) under Article L.123-35 of the French Commercial Code; the final administrative law appeal lies with the competent Tribunal Judiciaire within a further 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional permissibility: the SARL may establish its registered office at the manager's home for up to five years or with a licensed commercial domiciliation company under Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-138 of the French Commercial Code. A pure virtual office without physical records or human presence is not acceptable for an air cargo charter broker because the company must satisfy French customs record-keeping duties, DGAC operational supervision and the actual exercise of a commercial substance requirement for the ISIC 5229 activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 40% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation; the likelihood increases to about 65% if the company files UBO amendments or applies for a customs representative (RCD) status, due to targeted inspection programs by TRACFIN, French Customs (Direction générale des douanes) and the Civil Aviation Authority inspection unit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name pre-clearance and INPI trademark availability search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official INPI online tariff plus standard Parisian avocat fixed-rate IP clearance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and legal review of the French Articles of Association (statuts) of the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Avocat in the Barreau de Paris or French notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard SARL formation work (approximately EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,500 excluding VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory legal notice (annonce légale) in an authorized periodical
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales approved by the local prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: French state-controlled insertion tariff based on number of published lines and authorized journal schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Capital deposit certificate and bank interim account administration for SARL initial capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Banque de France regulated bank or Caisse des Dépôts for capital blocking
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank administrative fee for delivery of the capital deposit attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic filing of incorporation (constitution) through the Guichet unique / RNE
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed official RNE fee schedule for company formation filings

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration to the RCS and issuance of the company registration certificate (extrait Kbis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (competent commercial registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for corporate registration under Article A.743-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) submission and registry maintenance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed RNE administrative fee for beneficial ownership statement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and French sanctions screening for UBOs, shareholders and proposed managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance technology provider or specialised compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per individual and per sanction list, three-list series included

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization and sworn French translation of foreign UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice competent authority or French mission abroad plus sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee plus French consular tariff and transcript fixed rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service for 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market rate for a professionally staffed address, mail handling and regulatory visitor reception

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary aviation and customs regulatory opinion for air cargo charter brokerage (ISIC 5229)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal-retainer benchmark for pre-incorporation sector-specific advisory work including DGAC and customs representativity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II — Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (S.A.R.L.); Article L.223-7 (minimum 20% immediate payment-up of subscribed capital); Articles L.123-1 to L.123-32 and Decree n° 84-406 of 30 April 1984 (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Order n° 2021-1390 (Guichet Unique E-formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique Électronique of the INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle), routing to the territorial Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce administering the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire Cerfa n° 14785 (Formulaire M0) — Déclaration de création d'une personne morale, filed digitally through guichet-procedures.inpi.fr with the mandatory annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a SARL; the capital is freely fixed in the Articles of Association. The subscribed capital must be fully subscribed, and at least one-fifth (20%) must be paid up on incorporation (Art. L.223-7), with the balance payable within five years. Funds must be deposited with a French credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the depositary issues an escrow certificate of deposit valid until the Kbis registration, upon which the funds are released. Recommended capital for commercial and DREAL financial-standing purposes: €10,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned associates constitute a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under Book II of the French Commercial Code and fully subscribe the share capital of €10,000, divided into 1,000 shares of €10 each, deposited in escrow with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, at least 20% being paid upon incorporation and the remainder within five years. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [address], Paris, France. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Gérant for an unlimited term, with full powers to register the company, open escrow and bank accounts, publish the legal notice, obtain all freight-forwarding registrations, and sign all corporate documents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French General Directorate of Public Finance, under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. Primary portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr; business registration single-window portal (Guichet Unique) operated by INPI: https://procedures.inpi.fr; customs and export control authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed French SARL: (i) file incorporation with the Guichet Unique electronic portal to obtain SIREN (9-digit INSEE identification number) and SIRET (establishment code); (ii) upon SIREN issuance, the DGFiP automatically allocates the French intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) with format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN where the entity files an activity declaration (déclaration d'existence) with the competent SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises); (iii) foreign non-established entities performing taxable transactions in France must register directly with the DGFiP Non-Resident Unit (Unité de Gestion des Impositions des Non-Résidents, 10 rue du Centre, Noisy-le-Grand) using form No. 3826-SD (VAT) or via the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) in the Member State of establishment for distance sales of goods; (iv) documentary package for non-resident registration: certified articles of association, certificate of foreign tax residence, power of attorney for the appointed fiscal representative (for non-EU principals), director's passport and proof of address, and bank statements evidencing the operating account in France or the client country; (v) the SARL must also file the annual beneficial-owner declaration (RBE - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) and obtain an EORI number (GBC-000-XXXXX) for customs operations through the DGDDI portal SOPRANO Pro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés - IS) at the standard rate of 25%, with a reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below €10 million); resident entities are taxed on worldwide profits, while foreign companies are taxed in France exclusively on profits attributable to a French permanent establishment (établissement stable); dividends received benefit from the 95% participation-exemption (régime mère-fille) subject to a 5% taxable fraction, and profits repatriated by a foreign parent are subject to a 30% withholding tax on distributions absent treaty relief. Air cargo charter brokerage revenue is treated as taxable service income in France unless the place-of-supply rules (Articles 259 to 259 D CGI) assign the taxable event outside France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) Option for partnership taxation under Article 239 bis AA CGI enabling a SARL to be taxed transparently at the shareholder level (Impôt sur le Revenu) for a maximum duration of five fiscal years where the company is dedicated to a defined activity (e.g., specialized brokerage) and all qualifying shareholders consent; (ii) fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI allowing a French parent holding at least 95% of the SARL to consolidate the SARL's results in a group tax return — optional but binding for five years; (iii) option under Article 219 CGI for small and medium companies to retain the 15% reduced IS rate; (iv) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C III CGI for closely linked French entities; (v) hybrid mismatch declarations under Article 212 bis CGI and DAC-6 (Directive 2011/16/EU as amended) requiring disclosure of hybrid instruments and reverse-hybrid arrangements; elections are filed with the competent SIE by the tax return filing deadline (generally 30 April of the following year via EFI/EDI platform).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA) as codified in Articles 256 to 298 ter of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established French SARL: the 'franchise en base de TVA' (small-business VAT exemption) applies only below €91,900 annual turnover for goods and €36,800 for services (2025 thresholds, with reduced ceilings of €39,100 and €18,900 after two consecutive years above the standard threshold); once the threshold is exceeded, full VAT registration is mandatory from the first transaction of the exceeding month. Non-established foreign entities: NO registration threshold applies — any taxable B2B or B2C transaction performed in France triggers immediate VAT registration, although B2B services supplied by a non-resident broker to a French VAT-registered client are effectively shifted to the client via the reverse-charge (autoliquidation) mechanism under Article 283-2 CGI; EU-established sellers may use the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) regime for distance sales when their EU-wide turnover is below the €10,000 electronic-commerce micro-threshold; air cargo charter brokerage services are B2B in nature and thus subject to reverse charge where the customer is a taxable person established in France, while services to non-EU clients fall outside French VAT under the place-of-supply rule of Article 259 B CGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is deploying a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting framework under Articles 289 bis CGI and Decree No. 2022-1299: (i) from 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices in the standard formats (Factur-X hybrid PDF/XML, UBL, or CII), and large and mid-size companies (grandes et moyennes entreprises) must issue them; (ii) from 1 September 2027 all small and micro entities (PME/TPE) must issue e-invoices and transmit transaction data through a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) connected to the public clearing portal PPF (Portail Public de Facturation); (iii) clearance is near-real-time — transaction data must be transmitted to the PPF within 1 working day of invoice issuance, including e-reporting data for B2C sales, intra-Community supplies, and export transactions; (iv) digital stamping and integrity requirements mandate a qualified electronic signature (cachet de l'opérateur) or a secure business-data exchange network; (v) non-compliance penalties under Article 1731 ter CGI: €15 per non-compliant invoice (capped at €15,000 per calendar year), and 5% of the transaction amount (50% for fraud) for failure to transmit e-reporting data. The SARL cargo charter broker must ensure its invoicing platform is Factur-X compliant and connected to an authorized PDP before the 1 September 2026 obligation date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération avec droit à déduction / TVA au taux 0%) is available under: (i) Article 262-1 CGI for goods physically exported outside the European Union provided dispatch occurs within 90 days of supply and proof of exit is retained; (ii) Article 262-2 CGI for ancillary and brokering services directly connected to exported goods, including air cargo transport, charter brokerage, loading, handling, and freight-forwarding services rendered to the exporter or to the carrier of the exported goods; (iii) Article 259 B CGI provides that B2B services supplied by the French SARL broker to a client established in a non-EU country are outside the territorial scope of French VAT (i.e., deemed zero-rate), irrespective of where the goods travel, provided the recipient is a taxable person acting as such and the intermediary service is legally distinct from the underlying agreement; (iv) intra-Community supply of goods to EU clients may also qualify for exemption under Article 262-1-1 CGI subject to Greek Union sales-list filing; the broker must retain contractual evidence (charter party agreement, agency or brokerage contract, air waybill) demonstrating the direct link between the brokerage service and the physical export movement, and must verify the customer's non-EU VAT status through reliable commercial databases.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / Déclaration Administrative Unique) lodged electronically via the DELTA-X / ECS module of SOPRANO Pro, bearing the customs office master reference and export date
Air Waybill (LTA - Lettre de Transport Aérien) or Master Bill of Lading evidencing the cargo movement from France to a non-EU destination
Commercial Invoice and Charter Party or Brokerage Contract stating the place of supply, service description, and the non-EU status of the counterparty
Proof of Physical Exit and Delivery (destination customs entry proof, consignee delivery receipt, carrier cargo manifest, or port/airport authority stamped documentation)

Inward Remittance Certificate (bordereau de rapatriement) — bank SWIFT credit confirmation or transfer receipt evidencing settlement from the non-French counterparty within the commercial credit period
Packing List and Cargo Manifest / Master House Manifest certification where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and DGDDI jointly verify export zero-rating claims through the Enquête Export internal control program and customs post-clearance audits. Failure to produce the statutory export proof within the required window triggers: (i) VAT reassessment at the standard 20% rate plus intérêts de retard at 0.2% per month under Article 1727 CGI (2.4% per annum); (ii) a 5% late-payment surcharge if assessed tax remains unpaid after 30 days; (iii) a 40% penalty for bad-faith understatement (mauvaise foi) and 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers (manœuvre frauduleuse) under Article 1729 CGI; (iv) customs sanctions under Articles 414 to 423 of the Code des Douanes, including fines from one to three times the tax evaded, confiscation of the goods or transport equipment, and imprisonment up to 5 years in cases of organized fraud; (v) retrospective clawback extends 3 fiscal years (6 years in the presence of fraud or undeclared activity, and up to 10 years for non-registered operations); (vi) the SARL and its gérant are jointly and severally liable for assessed duties; denial of zero-rating also severs related input VAT recovery and may trigger the interest charge and publication of corrective tax returns (fondations).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full capital account convertibility and current account convertibility under EU regulations. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted, subject solely to standard corporate tax compliance, beneficial ownership declarations, and anti-money laundering verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds applies. Air cargo charter receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts without conversion. There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio; proceeds may be used freely for operational purposes after standard documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business or Revolut Corporate are feasible for French SARL entities with full KYC/AML compliance; however, legal constraints include mandatory transaction reporting, potential restrictions on high-volume air cargo settlements, and limited integration with traditional SWIFT rails for international freight payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for French SARL entities via video KYC, digital identification, and power of attorney; physical presence of directors is not mandatory for standard onboarding but may be required for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 or enhanced due diligence reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership involving non-EU entities or inconsistent source of funds declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of director identification documents, corporate charter, board resolutions authorizing the account opening, proof of ultimate beneficial owners, and detailed transaction purpose explanations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification requires supporting documentation including board resolutions, bank statements, and source of funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for air cargo charter settlements cleared via SWIFT MT103 or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit. All payments require matching trade contracts, invoices, and compliance with anti-money laundering regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual deposit of statutory financial statements (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements, and in all cases no later than seven months after the end of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a formal notice; continued default after one month exposes the company to an administrative fine of up to EUR 4,500, an injunction from the president of the commercial court, and ultimately administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and supporting liasse fiscale (form 2065 with annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period, the second working day after 1 May of the following year; online filing follows the same statutory calendar rule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic penalty on assessed corporate income tax, increased to 40% after a formal demand and 80% in proven deliberate understatement; late-payment interest is added at 0.2% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation tax balance payment (solde d'impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year closing on 31 December, by 15 May of the following year; for non-calendar year-ends, by the 15th day of the third month following the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 5% late-payment penalty plus interest at 0.2% per month; formal enforcement measures are initiated after an unsuccessful payment notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CVAE/CET annual declaration (cotisation sur la valeur ajoutée des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, the second working day after 1 May of the following year; no CVAE declaration is due where annual turnover excluding VAT is below EUR 152,500.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission is subject to the same 10%/40%/80% graduated administrative penalties and 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; the tax authority may reassess the tax base after a formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be confirmed no later than the date of the shareholders' meeting approving the annual accounts and in any case before the annual accounts filing deadline; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the beneficial-owner declaration exposes the company to a formal notice, administrative fine up to EUR 7,500 for a legal entity, and an adverse RCS mention that may lead to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor must be appointed for an SARL if, at the close of a financial year and for two of the three immediately preceding years, two of the following thresholds are exceeded: total balance sheet assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average permanent staff above 50 employees. In addition, minority shareholders representing at least one-tenth of the share capital may obtain a court-ordered statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan comptable général, PCG) as codified by the Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC) and the Code de commerce; IFRS is permitted for voluntary consolidated statements if the company is in a group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Articles L.561-46 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code, the SARL must file the initial beneficial-owner declaration (DBE) with the RCS and thereafter update it within 30 days of any change. Every year, before the annual accounts are deposited, the manager must confirm in the registry that the beneficial-owner data remains accurate. Any share transfer must be recorded in the share-movement ledger and, if the transfer causes any individual to hold or control at least 25% of the share capital or voting rights, the beneficial-owner declaration must be updated within the same 30-day window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share-transfer ledger (registre des mouvements de titres)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject generally to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. France has no general corporate tax holiday. Qualifying research and development may benefit from the 30% research tax credit in metropolitan France, subject to statutory conditions. Certain income and capital gains may qualify for participation-exemption or patent-box treatment, subject to specific requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the DGFiP EDI-TDFC channel or an authorized tax software provider, with supporting tax tables including Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and applicable credit, finance, and related-party schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; corporate income tax instalments are generally payable quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the electronic return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the annual DGFiP filing calendar. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, principal activity, financial year dates, tax office, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SARL's French legal identity and SIREN. A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the French taxpayer; the French SARL reports its worldwide taxable result subject to French domestic law and applicable treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, taxable result and tax calculation section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, corporate income tax due, instalments, tax credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the result calculated under French tax rules, including required add-backs, deductible expenses, foreign-source income, permanent establishments, and tax credits. Apply treaty relief only through the relevant statutory mechanism and retain supporting certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss reconciled to taxable profit or loss through permanent and temporary adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible expenses, including unsupported management charges, excessive interest, penalties, and private expenditure. Deduct qualifying exempt or separately taxed items and document foreign-related adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses utilized, carried forward, or potentially carried back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French losses are generally carried forward without a time limit but utilization is capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding year and EUR 1 million, subject to election and statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit, including participation and distribution-related information where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose distributions and relevant shareholder information consistently with corporate records, dividend resolutions, and withholding tax filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, depreciable assets, non-depreciable assets, securities, and special tax treatments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify asset disposals, securities transactions, and participation-exemption claims. Maintain acquisition costs, holding-period evidence, valuation support, and treaty documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit and other applicable tax credits or reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits for qualifying French activities and retain contemporaneous technical, personnel, expenditure, and allocation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specified categories of non-deductible expenses, including certain vehicle, luxury, representation, and management expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose expenses that are non-deductible under French rules, even where booked in accounts and paid to foreign suppliers or related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of related-party transactions and transfer pricing policy where the statutory threshold or other triggering conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with related entities, transaction categories, jurisdictions, amounts, and pricing methods. Reconcile the declaration to the general ledger, statutory accounts, and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and other investment income paid to non-residents where French withholding applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File and pay electronically, generally by the 15th day of the month following payment or distribution. Apply treaty or EU relief only after verifying beneficial ownership, residence, anti-abuse, ownership, holding-period, and procedural requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete corporate income tax filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% in cases of deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% in specified abusive or fraudulent circumstances. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Insufficient transfer pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of the statutory minimum or 0.5% of the amount of transactions covered by missing documentation, with additional reassessment, interest, and penalties. Failure to file required foreign-account or foreign-asset information may generate separate penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. A qualifying EU parent may generally obtain a 0% rate where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse, and documentary conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements, minimum ownership and holding-period conditions, and the absence of a French permanent establishment to which the income is attributable. Use the applicable French relief-at-source procedure or refund procedure, including the relevant treaty form where required. Retain the residence certificate, ownership chart, dividend resolution, payment evidence, recipient declaration, and anti-abuse analysis. File Form 2777-SD and remit any withholding by the statutory deadline. Relief must not be applied solely on the basis of incorporation or an intermediary payment address.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief, and special rules for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. French domestic withholding on ordinary interest paid to non-residents is generally 0%, although anti-abuse provisions, payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, hybrid mismatch rules, beneficial ownership requirements, and treaty provisions may alter the result. Treaty rates are country-specific and must be verified against the applicable France treaty. Royalties and interest must be supported by arm's-length agreements, beneficial ownership evidence, tax residence certificates, and withholding filings.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million is the principal threshold for mandatory comprehensive transfer pricing documentation, generally applying where the French entity or French tax group reaches the statutory turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where the entity is owned or controlled by an entity meeting the threshold. The documentation generally comprises a Master File and Local File and must be available to the French tax authority upon request. A separate annual simplified transfer pricing declaration on Form 2257-SD is generally triggered at EUR 50 million turnover or gross assets, or by specified ownership, control, or transaction conditions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless essential under the French general anti-abuse doctrine, abuse-of-law rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, treaty anti-abuse provisions, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid mismatch rules, and permanent-establishment principles. A French SARL should maintain French commercial rationale, decision-making, personnel or appropriately controlled outsourced functions, premises or operational capacity, bank and accounting records, risk control, and contemporaneous evidence that the air-cargo brokerage activity is actually performed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing brokerage commissions, underreporting charter margins, fabricating invoices, using false supplier contracts, diverting customer receipts, or deliberately omitting taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, surcharges up to 80% in specified fraudulent or abusive cases, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment and substantial fines. Aggravated tax fraud can attract imprisonment of up to seven years and a fine of up to EUR 3 million for individuals, subject to statutory conditions and judicial determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability to the company or creditors, management bans, and tax-liability proceedings where fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct causes non-payment. Imprisonment is not automatic. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction but may arise from judicial measures or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, and beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a nominal holding company lacking personnel, decision-making, commercial risk, or beneficial ownership, or claiming treaty relief without substantive entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU relief, withholding tax assessment, interest, 40% or 80% penalties where applicable, general anti-abuse or abuse-of-law adjustments, and possible criminal exposure where false declarations or fraudulent structures are established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving sham structures or false certificates may face personal criminal and civil exposure, management restrictions, and liability for resulting tax losses where statutory conditions for personal liability are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpaying related-party charter, insurance, financing, management, or technology charges; stripping French profits through unsupported commissions; or failing to document controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment, denial of deductions, withholding or recharacterization of payments, documentation penalties, late-payment interest, and tax surcharges. The documentation penalty may be based on the statutory minimum or a percentage of the transactions covered by missing or incomplete documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate profit diversion, insolvency-related liability, and criminal liability if documentation is knowingly falsified or the arrangement forms part of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing false invoices, claiming input VAT on fictitious charter services, misclassifying international transport, failing to account for reverse-charge VAT, or using missing-trader arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, recovery of improperly refunded VAT, late-payment interest, penalties potentially reaching 40% or 80%, invoice penalties, and criminal prosecution for organized or fraudulent conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally liable in cases of fraudulent VAT conduct, deliberate participation, or serious management fault, in addition to criminal sanctions and possible management bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, sanctions, export-control, and aviation-security breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arranging air cargo involving prohibited goods, sanctioned parties, embargoed destinations, inaccurate commodity classification, false customs value or origin, or cargo handled without required regulated-agent or aviation-security controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, VAT, seizure, administrative sanctions, loss of authorizations, transaction prohibitions, substantial fines, and criminal penalties under French, EU customs, sanctions, export-control, and aviation-security law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment where applicable, professional disqualification, and civil claims. Travel bans may be imposed only through applicable judicial or administrative measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting opaque payments, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions screening, structuring payments, or processing funds inconsistent with the customer's business profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement, reporting obligations to TRACFIN where applicable, administrative fines, criminal money-laundering penalties, confiscation, and suspension or loss of professional authorizations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for laundering, complicity, failure to prevent or report qualifying conduct, or deliberate compliance failures. Imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and management bans may apply; travel restrictions depend on judicial orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed or improperly operated freight-forwarding and transport-intermediary activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing regulated transport-intermediary or freight-forwarding functions without required French registration, professional capacity, financial standing, insurance, security authorization, or customs representation status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, fines, prohibition from operating, withdrawal of registration or authorization, contract and insurance consequences, and criminal sanctions where the underlying conduct constitutes an offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for knowingly operating without required authorization, misleading customers or authorities, or causing safety, customs, or financial harm. Civil damages, management bans, and criminal penalties may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying related parties while insolvent, transferring assets below value, preferring insiders, continuing operations while knowingly unable to pay debts, or distributing funds while statutory creditor protections are impaired.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, insolvency proceedings, extension of insolvency liability, bankruptcy-related sanctions, fines, and potential imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or asset concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to company liabilities, prohibited from managing companies, and prosecuted for mismanagement or fraudulent bankruptcy. Civil restitution and confiscation may apply. Travel bans are possible only where ordered under applicable judicial procedures.
